source: Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — booklet 'ដំណាំពោត' (Corn Crop), Issue 1, 2003, funded by Asian Development Bank (ADB), Loan/Grant No. 1445-CAM(SF), section I: Status of corn in Cambodia
text:
Corn is a crop that has been known and cultivated in Cambodia for over 17 centuries, grown in various forms throughout the country as food to supplement rice as the staple. This crop has high nutritional value and is one of the top 10 most important food crops in the world, ranking behind rice in Cambodia among countries where it is grown alongside rice and used to help address food security.

Cambodia also grows a glutinous/waxy corn variety with a growth cycle of about 40 days from planting to maturity. This corn is believed to have come to Cambodia via merchants who brought it from neighboring countries, later becoming a locally grown crop across regions and some producing areas.

Red corn (ពោតក្រហម) began to be widely known after 1921, when it was carried by Vietnamese and American traders into Cambodia. Later, propagation was promoted by the Department of Agriculture around 1930, which produced the Khmer red corn variety, a fast/short-cycle variety of about 40 days, with a stem base diameter of about 20cm, oval-shaped and short cob (about 8mm), pale yellow to orange-red kernel color on the upper part and dark red/maroon at the base. This corn is currently used for snacks and animal feed, and processed into other uses as well. Development of new corn varieties has since been carried out with assistance from Phnom Penh and Kampong Cham province.

American-origin field corn (ពោតផ្កែម), which is commonly used as poultry/animal feed and also eaten as a snack when boiled or roasted, is another type grown in Cambodia, with a growth cycle around a few months.

Corn is considered one of the important crops among all cereal grain crops grown in Cambodia. According to a corn production trend, it is estimated that from the year 2000 corn cultivation and yield expanded to become the number-1 crop in the world by area (note: this figure as read from the source is unclear/possibly a transcription of a broader global corn-production statistic and should be treated as approximate). In 1996, corn-growing area/production in the corn production sector reached 63.5 thousand tons.
